packs.title: Paths and Water
packs.promise: Read another Copenhagen through patterned paving, western gardens and harbour structures.

q.s: Find three different turns in a patterned square.
st: From a comfortable stopped position, find three changes in the white paving lines: a tight bend, a broad sweep and a line interrupted by an object.
Give each change a rhythm using your own short words or marks. Leave all objects and paving untouched.
Choose the rhythm that would make the best opening to an imaginary walk and save your three-part collection.

q.s: Make an original pattern from a winding garden.
st: Find a curved water edge, a patch of open lawn and a cluster of trees from one stopped visitor path. Use the official garden photograph with water, lawn and trees instead if preferred.
On your own paper or device, assign each element a different abstract mark: a curve, a gap or a cluster of dots. Arrange the three into an original small score.
Read the score from left to right and write one sentence about its imagined pace. Save your marks or describe their order in words.

q.s: Design a small message from a waterside structure.
st: From the public promenade, choose three ingredients for an original postcard: one bold built shape, one open-water space and one small movement.
Make a small original composition using words or simple marks. Give the bold shape one corner and leave deliberate blank space for the water.
Add a short message of your own about the direction the scene invites your eye to take, then save your postcard.

packs.title: Colour and Calm
packs.promise: Gather a small palette of Copenhagen, from coloured facades to quieter garden details.

q.s: Gather a three-colour palette at Nyhavn.
st: Choose a comfortable public view along the coloured house fronts beside Nyhavn.
Collect three colours from the facades, roof surfaces or window frames. Nothing needs to be picked up.
Give each colour a name of your own and arrange the three from warmest to coolest.
Save the palette and choose one colour to notice again later in the chapter.

q.s: Write a tiny caption for Gråbrødretorv.
st: Find a comfortable view that includes the square’s large tree and a coloured facade behind it.
Choose one leaf or branch shape and one window or roof edge. Write an original six-word caption joining those details.
Change just one word to give the caption a different pace or mood.
Save both versions and choose the one you would keep.

q.s: Find three quiet repetitions at Amalienborg.
st: Choose a comfortable position in the square with a clear view of one palace facade, away from guards, entrances and routes in use.
Find three pairs: two windows, two upright facade divisions and two sloping roof lines.
Choose the pair that feels most alike. Describe one small difference caused by light, angle or a visible detail.
Save your three pairs and the difference you noticed.
